statement: Let P be an L-periodic locally finite point process, Q a bounded centered fundamental parallelepiped, G a nonzero reciprocal vector and 0<q=E N(Q)<infinity. With m=E sum_{x in X intersect Q} exp(i G dot x) and D=E sum_{x in X intersect Q}(G dot x)^2, Re m>=q-D/2; D<2q implies P is not invariant under all translations.
assumptions: L-periodicity of the law is an assumption
Q is a fundamental parallelepiped centered at the fixed crystal phase
G dot L is contained in 2*pi*Z
proof_or_counterexample: Integrate cos(t)>=1-t^2/2 against the local intensity; a fully stationary intensity is rho times Lebesgue and its nonzero reciprocal Fourier coefficient over Q vanishes.
remaining_gap: No periodic Riesz Gibbs law or full-Gibbs moment estimate has been constructed; thermodynamic limit and removal of pinning remain unproved.

statement: For any grand-canonical DLR point process with nonnegative pair interactions, finite beta, finite activity a=exp(beta*mu), and m disjoint cells of volume at most v, P(all m cells occupied)<=(1-exp(-a*v))^m. Thus for countably many such cells, P(every cell has exactly one particle)=0. This applies to unpinned short-range Riesz gases s>d with the usual grand-canonical specification.
assumptions: H_D consists solely of nonnegative pair interactions and H_D(empty)=0
the stated grand-canonical DLR kernel exists
cells are pairwise disjoint with uniformly bounded volume
proof_or_counterexample: 1<=Z_D<=exp(a|D|), so the exterior-conditioned vacancy probability is >=exp(-a|D|). The previous cells' occupancy event is measurable outside the next cell, allowing sequential tower-property induction. Decreasing-event continuity completes the infinite-family conclusion.
remaining_gap: Long-range background terms and canonical number constraints prevent automatic extension. Periodic Gibbs phases with defects are not excluded.
proof_independence: Derived before paired proof read; no independent theorem check yet.

statement: For laws P_n of locally finite point measures converging weakly in the vague topology to P, a bounded fundamental cell Q with P(N(boundary Q)=0)=1 and uniformly integrable counts N_n(Q) ensure convergence of the expected count and expected local Fourier sum for any fixed reciprocal vector G. A strictly positive limiting real Fourier expectation survives; if all P_n share L-periodicity, the limit also does and cannot be fully stationary.
assumptions: weak convergence in the vague topology
bounded Q and no boundary particles under P
fixed lattice, phase and reciprocal vector
positive Fourier margin for the symmetry-breaking conclusion
proof_or_counterexample: Continuous mapping at point measures charging no boundary, |Fourier sum|<=N(Q), and uniform integrability give expectation convergence. Lattice translations are continuous, so their invariance passes to the limit.
remaining_gap: No Gibbs specification is passed by this lemma; DLR passage and actual Riesz moment/order estimates remain separate.

statement: For n>=3, independently activate each Z^3 cell with probability 1/n and place n points z+(j/n^2)e_1, j=1,...,n, in each activated cell. These simple Z^3-periodic laws have E N(Q)=1 and local reciprocal Fourier expectations tending to 1, but converge vaguely in law to the empty process whose Fourier expectation is zero. Thus bounded first moments do not suffice to preserve local Fourier order under weak convergence.
assumptions: independent cell activation is explicitly part of this constructed process
no claim that the counterexample laws are Riesz Gibbs laws
proof_or_counterexample: Any compact set meets finitely many cells, with activation probability at most their number/n. Expected count is n*(1/n)=1, and the normalized Fourier sum tends to 1 as all offsets tend to 0. For n>K, E[N(Q)1_{N(Q)>K}]=1, explicitly violating uniform integrability.
remaining_gap: Counterexample targets a convergence inference, not P0309; uniform higher local moments would exclude it.
